Match each grade from List I with the appropriate application from List II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.questionText: List-I contains viscosity grades of bitumen. List-II provides their typical applications. Match each grade from List I with the appropriate application from List II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanationHtml:
(a)
(i) VG10 : Spraying applications; paving applications in cold regions in lieu of 80/100 penetration grade.
(ii) VG20 : Paving applications in cold climatic conditions of North India and in high altitude regions.
(iii) VG30 : Paving applications for most part of India, in lieu of 60/70 penetration grade.
(iv) VG40 : Use in high stressed areas like intersections, toll plazas, truck terminals, truck laybyes
in lieu of 30/40 penetration grade.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: Considering the changes in declination (known as variation), which of the following statements is correct?
questions.questionText: Considering the changes in declination (known as variation), which of the following statements is correct?

options.html: Diurnal variation of declination is more for the places near the equator.
options.text: Diurnal variation of declination is more for the places near the equator.

options.html: Diurnal variation of declination is more in winter and less in summer.
options.text: Diurnal variation of declination is more in winter and less in summer.

options.html: In secular variation, the magnetic meridian swings like a pendulum.
options.text: In secular variation, the magnetic meridian swings like a pendulum.

options.html: Annual variation is generally observed to be of order of 1°.
options.text: Annual variation is generally observed to be of order of 1°.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
(i) Diurnal variation : Due to rotation of Earth about its axis.
• More in day time, less in night.
• More in summer, less in winter.
• More at poles, less on equator.
(ii) Annual variation : Due to revolution of Earth about Sun. Generally, observed to be 1-2 minutes.
(iii) Secular variation : Magnetic flux lines swing like a pendulum.
(iv) Irregular variation : Due to magnetic disturbances or storms. Generally, observed in order of 1°.
